messages.subject: Re: GoNoGo-hopefully easy question -data structure
messages.body_plain:
Hi Franziska,

which R version hBayesDM version, and rstan version do you use?

I am using R 3.4.1, hBayesDM 0.4.0, rstan 16.2. I am able to read your data file and can also run the model.

You can ignore the warnings though, because Stan now suggests using '//' instead of '#' for comment. Other than that, I suspect it is more a Stan problem. I suggest running the 8school example as described here <https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started>.

Hope it helps,
Lei

---
Lei Zhang
lei-zhang.net <http://lei-zhang.net/>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Franziska,

I saw your last post–are you still having trouble running the example models in hBayesDM? If so, have you tried testing rstan itself first? Sometimes, if rstan is not installed correctly or is missing a dependency, you will get strange parser errors such as the one you posted.

To test this, I would try running an example from the stan website: https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started

Best,
Nate

messages.subject: Jacobian adjustment term for logit-transformed estimation (ra_prospect, ra_noLA, ra_noRA)
messages.subject_clean: Jacobian adjustment term for logit-transformed estimation (ra_prospect, ra_noLA, ra_noRA)
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Thank you to the creators for putting together this great package! It's been invaluable while learning to implement STAN models.

I'm currently focused on extracting subjective preference parameters via STAN, as implemented in hBayesDM/ra_prospect. While researching the topic, I found this article (http://mc-stan.org/users/documentation/case-studies/mle-params.html) describing the importance/impact of including the Jacobian term when calculating Bayesian estimates on logit transformed variables. I'm still pretty new to STAN, but it appears the hBayesDM implementations of ra_prospect, ra_noLA, and ra_noRA don't include this term.

I'm trying to wrap my head around the validity of including the Jacobian adjustment, and would greatly appreciate if anyone could provide insight to why it is not included in the hBayesDM implementation.

Thank you for your help,
Joe
